The severe impairment—like getting written up at work and withdrawing from my family—actually happens during my low periods, not the high ones.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a high-energy episode that was severe enough to require hospitalization or cause significant problems in your relationships or at work, rather than just being a period of heightened productivity and impulsivity?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never been hospitalized for those high-energy times. While I did some impulsive things like overspending on credit cards, sending late-night work emails, and getting snappy when questioned, they didn't cause severe disruptions. They've never stretched out to two weeks or caused a major breakdown in my daily life while they were happening. The severe disruptions and problems with my work and family really only happen when I crash back down into the low periods.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there have been any periods where you felt completely normal, without either the high-energy symptoms or the depressive symptoms, lasting for at least two months, within the past year?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any long stretches of feeling normal like that over the past year. For about the last eleven months, I've felt stuck in some level of depression, and the only breaks I've had are those brief, high-energy bursts rather than any real time of feeling balanced.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether these cycles of high and low periods have been consistent over the past year, or have there been any changes in their frequency, duration, or severity over time?\n\nPatient: They’ve been happening off and on for about a year, but they have really come into focus and felt much more disruptive over this past month. For most of the last eleven months, I've just felt stuck in this low, depressed state, with only those brief, revved-up bursts breaking it up. It feels like the impact of these cycles is getting heavier.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks without any intervening high-energy episodes, and if so, how did those episodes compare in severity to your current state?\n\nPatient: Yes, my low periods last much longer than two weeks; I feel like I've been stuck in this depression for most of the past eleven months with only those brief, high-energy breaks. This current low stretch over the past month has been much more severe and harder to handle than before. It's actually the worst it's been, especially since it led to that formal warning at work.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe the shortest and longest duration of your depressive episodes over the past year, and how often these episodes have occurred, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?\n\nPatient: The longest depressive episode is definitely this current one, which has been hanging over me for most of the past eleven months, only interrupted by those brief, week-long high bursts. These ups and downs have been happening off and on for about a year now, but I haven't kept track of the specific number of times they've switched.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to approximate or recall roughly how many times you've switched between these high-energy and low, depressive states over the past year, even if it's not an exact count?\n\nPatient: It hasn't really been a constant, rapid switching back and forth. It's hard to count them precisely because the low feelings have felt almost continuous over the past year, with only those brief breaks of high energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to recall if there have been at least four distinct episodes where you switched between feeling extremely high or extremely low within the past 12 months, to help us better understand your condition?\n\nPatient: I'm really not sure of the exact number of times it has happened, as I haven't kept a precise count of the shifts. I just know that these ups and downs have been happening off and on for about a year now.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific events, dates, or periods that might help you or me estimate how many times you've switched between these high-energy and low, depressive states over the past year, even if it's not an exact count?\n\nPatient: The clearest switch was about a month ago, when I had that high-energy week of staying up late working on projects and then immediately crashed into this current low period that led to my work warning. Other than that, I’ve just felt stuck in some level of depression since late last year, only interrupted by a couple of other brief, revved-up bursts. These cycles have been happening off and on for about a year, but it's mostly just been that one long low period with those few quick peaks.\n\nDoctor: Can you think back over the past year and try to estimate or recall roughly how many distinct episodes of either high energy or depression you've experienced, even if you can't pinpoint exact dates or durations, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?\n\nPatient: Over the past year, these cycles of highs and lows have been happening off and on. I've felt stuck in a low, depressed state for most of the past eleven months, but that long stretch has been broken up by brief, week-long bursts where I suddenly feel overly revved up and high-energy.\n\nDoctor: Can you try to recall or estimate the total number of distinct episodes, either high-energy or depressive, you've experienced over the past year, to help us differentiate between potential diagnoses?"

I’ve completely lost interest in things I normally love, like fishing and gardening, and even the simplest tasks feel like I'm wading through deep mud.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing this feeling of hopelessness and loss of interest in activities, is it something that's been going on for a few weeks, months, or has it been coming and going over a longer period?\n\nPatient: This low, hopeless feeling has actually been hanging over me since late last year, so I've been stuck in this depression for about eleven months now with only brief breaks. These overall cycles of ups and downs have been going on off and on for about a year, but it's really come to a head over this past month.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these brief breaks you've had from the depressive feelings, were they spontaneous or triggered by something, and how long did they typically last?\n\nPatient: Those breaks are actually phases where I feel the exact opposite—really revved up, full of energy, and on top of the world for about a week or so. They seem to just happen on their own as part of a cycle rather than being triggered by anything specific. These cycles of crashing into these drained stretches have been happening off and on for about a year now.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate the total number of days or weeks you've spent in these high-energy episodes versus the low, depressive episodes over the past year to help understand the balance between these states?\n\nPatient: The low, depressive periods have taken up the vast majority of the past year, leaving me feeling stuck in a depression for about eleven months.
